newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends mixed on technicals.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends mixed on technicals.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended mixed after technical adjustments by local producers trying to compete against regional prices, traders said.
However, absence of keen consumer demand kept the market in the doldrums, and no inquiries or sales were noted through the day, the traders said.
"We can't compete against the Thai and Indonesian prices now, unless we bring our prices down further," a trader said.
At the close, February RSS1 buyer was quoted at 304 cents ($1.23) a kg by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board (MRELB), down half cent from Monday's close.
February SMR 20 was unchanged at 300 cents by the MRELB. Trading houses offered the SMR 20 at 299 cents a kg, SMR CV at 361, SMR L at 343, SMR 5 at 312, SMR 10 at 300 and drum latex FOB at 237.
The Malaysia market has drifted without keen demand since October last year after institutional consumers in the U.S. and Europe met most of their rubber requirements until March 1997.
The INRO five-day average was 234.92 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Jan 20 from 234.90 on Jan 17. The daily indicator was at 235.09 against 235.02 previously.
